q: A team sets overall materiality at 50 lakh and performance materiality at 35 lakh, and now must fix the clearly trivial threshold. Which statement best reflects SA 320 and SA 450?
o: A fixed 5 percent of performance materiality on each engagement
The smallest misstatement the planned procedures are able to detect
An amount below which items are inconsequential singly and together
A cap keeping accumulated trivial items below performance materiality
why: Clearly trivial is a judgement about items inconsequential individually and in aggregate by any criteria of size, nature or circumstances; percentage rules of thumb are conventions, not requirements.

q: Which best explains why performance materiality is set below overall materiality?
o: To leave headroom for undetected and uncorrected misstatements
To reduce sampling risk to zero across the transaction classes tested
Because SA 320 fixes it at exactly 75 percent of overall materiality
To give the auditor a basis for identifying clearly trivial items
why: Performance materiality creates headroom for misstatements the auditor does not detect and those left uncorrected; no fixed percentage is mandated and it is not the clearly trivial threshold.

q: An entity is a loss making start up with volatile profits but stable growing revenue and a large asset base. Using profit before tax as the benchmark would be inappropriate mainly because:
o: SA 320 bars profit before tax whenever a loss is reported
Revenue is the mandated benchmark for entities in a growth phase
Total assets must be used whenever assets exceed annual revenue
Near break even profit swings wildly and is an unstable base
why: SA 320 asks for a benchmark that is stable and relevant to users; near break even profit swings wildly, but no standard bans profit or mandates revenue or assets.

q: Materiality for particular classes of transactions, account balances or disclosures is set when:
o: The engagement partner prefers lower thresholds in all risk areas
Smaller misstatements in those items could still influence users
The client asks for separate thresholds on related party disclosures
A component auditor adopted lower materiality than the group auditor
why: SA 320 triggers a separate lower materiality only where users would be influenced by smaller misstatements in that area, such as related party transactions or directors remuneration.

q: Halfway through the audit the auditor learns that actual results will fall far short of the forecast used to compute planning materiality. Under SA 320 the auditor must:
o: Keep the original amount to preserve comparability of the file
Revise only if the change exceeds 10 percent of the original figure
Revise it and reconsider performance materiality and procedures
Revise only at completion when evaluating uncorrected misstatements
why: Revision is required when information emerges that would have led to a different amount initially, and planned procedures must then be reconsidered; there is no 10 percent trigger.

q: Which uncorrected misstatement is most likely to be judged material despite being far below overall materiality?
o: A misstatement that turns a small reported profit into a loss
An understatement of the accrual for office stationery expense
A reclassification between two expense heads in the profit statement
An overstatement of a debt that is already fully provided against
why: SA 450 requires qualitative evaluation, and a misstatement that flips profit to loss or affects covenants and bonuses is material by nature; the others lack that significance.

q: Under SA 450 the auditor must communicate uncorrected misstatements to those charged with governance and also:
o: Modify the opinion once they exceed performance materiality
Withdraw from the engagement where management refuses to correct them
Aggregate them with clearly trivial items before any comparison
Obtain a written representation that the effects are immaterial
why: SA 450 requires a written representation with a summary of the uncorrected items attached; clearly trivial items are excluded from accumulation and exceeding performance materiality is not itself an opinion trigger.

q: A misstatement of 12 lakh caused by a control failure in the purchase cycle is identified when overall materiality is 60 lakh, and management corrects it. Under SA 450 the auditor should:
o: Treat the matter as closed once the correcting entry is posted
Consider whether more misstatements exist and revise the plan
Increase overall materiality to reflect the corrected balances
Report the matter under section 143 12 as a suspected fraud case
why: SA 450 requires the auditor to consider whether an identified misstatement indicates that others exist and whether the approach must change; correction alone does not answer that, and a control failure is not automatically fraud.

q: Which statement about projected misstatement from audit sampling is correct in the SA 450 evaluation?
o: Only factual misstatements accumulate since projections are estimates
Projected amounts are compared with performance materiality alone
Projected items join factual and judgemental ones in the aggregate
Management may clear a projection by correcting the sampled items
why: SA 450 recognises factual, judgemental and projected misstatements and requires all three in the aggregate assessment; corrections must address the population, not just the sample.

q: A group auditor sets group materiality at 2 crore. For a component contributing 30 percent of consolidated revenue, component materiality should be:
o: Lower than group materiality to allow for aggregation risk
Exactly 30 percent of group materiality to mirror the revenue share
Equal to group materiality since the group is the reporting entity
Derived solely from the component standalone financial statements
why: Component materiality must sit below group materiality to allow for aggregation across components; a mechanical revenue share or a standalone only basis ignores that aggregation risk.

q: Which best describes the interaction between materiality and audit risk?
o: They vary directly, so higher materiality means higher audit risk
Materiality is fixed after audit risk and cannot influence it
Materiality affects only evaluation, never the planning of work
They are inverse, so lower materiality calls for more extensive work
why: A lower materiality means smaller misstatements matter, so detection risk must be lowered through more extensive or effective work; materiality is set at planning and drives nature, timing and extent.

q: A company has revenue of 100 crore, profit before tax of 40 lakh after one off director bonuses, and net assets of 60 crore. The most defensible benchmark choice is:
o: Profit before tax, the primary indicator for all commercial entities
Normalised profit before tax after the one off bonus adjustment
Total revenue at 5 percent, being the largest reported figure
Net assets, because equity holders are always the primary users
why: SA 320 permits normalising a benchmark for unusual one off items or selecting a more stable measure; using a distorted profit or simply picking the largest number is not reasoned selection.

q: Which is NOT an appropriate reason to set performance materiality at a lower percentage of overall materiality?
o: A history of numerous misstatements found in prior year audits
A first year audit with limited accumulated knowledge of the entity
A wish to limit testing and hold down the agreed audit fee
Significant deficiencies identified in the entity control environment
why: Performance materiality is lowered where the risk of undetected misstatement is higher, such as prior errors, first year audits or weak controls; commercial fee pressure is never a valid basis.

q: When misstatements identified during the audit are corrected by management, the auditor under SA 450 should still:
o: Communicate them and request correction of all non trivial items
Disregard them entirely once the correcting entries have been posted
Report them to the Registrar of Companies as accounting irregularities
Add them back when comparing the aggregate with overall materiality
why: SA 450 requires timely communication and a request to correct all accumulated misstatements; corrected items leave the uncorrected aggregate but the pattern may still signal control weaknesses.

q: Which situation best illustrates a judgemental misstatement under SA 450?
o: A sales invoice posted twice because of a keying error at entry
A shortfall extrapolated from a sample of inventory differences
An expense in the wrong period from a cut off failure at year end
A gap between the management credit loss and auditor estimate
why: Judgemental misstatements arise from differences over estimates or policy selection; duplicated invoices and cut off errors are factual and extrapolated shortfalls are projected.

q: In assessing the aggregate effect of uncorrected misstatements the auditor also considers prior period items because:
o: SA 450 requires every prior period misstatement to be corrected now
Carried forward items can reverse into current period results
Comparatives must be restated whenever an uncorrected item existed
Prior period misstatements lapse once the earlier report is issued
why: Uncorrected items carried forward can reverse into the current period and build up in balances, so the auditor weighs the effect on both current results and period end balances.

q: Materiality of 2.5 crore is derived from revenue of 500 crore and is challenged by the engagement quality reviewer. The strongest defence is:
o: The client agreed the amount when signing the engagement letter
The identical percentage was applied in the prior year audit file
Revenue is the relevant stable measure and the rate is accepted
It yields an efficient sample size for testing the revenue ledger
why: The justification must rest on relevance to users, stability of the benchmark and an appropriate percentage; client agreement, precedent and sampling efficiency are not valid grounds.

q: The aggregate of uncorrected misstatements is 48 lakh against overall materiality of 50 lakh. The most appropriate response is to:
o: Recognise that undetected items may push the total past materiality
Issue an unmodified opinion as the aggregate is below materiality
Qualify the opinion since the aggregate is close to materiality
Raise overall materiality to 60 lakh to restore proper headroom
why: SA 450 requires the auditor to consider that when the aggregate approaches materiality, undetected misstatements may push the total past it, so more work or correction is needed; raising materiality to accommodate errors is unacceptable.
